1:## Description
2:Dynamic Cheatsheet builds prompts from curated text or prior examples and carries returned text through caller or benchmark state; source wiring is visible, but use and benefit are unobserved.
4:## Bounded synthesis
6:At the registered repository revision, evidence is source inspection of the complete shipped repository; no live provider run or independent experiment was supplied ([boundary](boundary.md)). Dynamic Cheatsheet is an inference-time prompt and memory workflow: it leaves model parameters untouched in the inspected code and passes natural-language text or prior input/output examples into later model calls. The configured model first generates an answer; cumulative modes then ask it to propose a replacement cheatsheet. The parser accepts text marked with `<cheatsheet>` and otherwise retains the old text. The prompt requests correctness assessment, but code does not check that assessment or gate the write on the benchmark target ([RT-RTE-cumulative-loop](runtime.md), [MEM-RTE-cumulative-write](memory.md), [RT-OBJ-cheatsheet](runtime.md)).
8:The benchmark carries returned text across questions and saves rows that can be loaded on continuation. Its answer evaluator compares the answer with task-specific targets only after curation, updates counters, and does not admit, revise, or roll back the text. Other modes rank prior input/output pairs by cosine similarity over fixed precomputed vectors, synthesize selected examples into prompt text, append all prior examples, or use retrieved examples directly. The parts are distinct: linguistic example history and numeric selector vectors ([RT-RTE-checkpoint-resume](runtime.md), [EPI-RTE-benchmark-answer-check](epistemic.md), [MEM-OBJ-example-history](memory.md), [MEM-OBJ-embedding-table](memory.md), [RT-RTE-retrieval-synthesis](runtime.md), [RT-RTE-cumulative-retrieval](runtime.md), [RT-RTE-direct-retrieval](runtime.md), [RT-RTE-full-history](runtime.md)).
10:These mechanisms establish delivery and retention paths, not that a model relies on the delivered content, that curated or prior answers are correct, or that either improves later answers. The README's performance and learning claims are not established by the inspected implementation or supplied run evidence; target scores do not feed curation. The evidence therefore supports prompt-guided memory and context selection, while learning, improved capacity, and causal performance gains remain undemonstrated ([EPI-CLM-performance-gains](epistemic.md), [EPI-CLM-zero-shot-learning](epistemic.md), [RT-RTE-cumulative-loop](runtime.md)).
12:The repository also exposes local Python execution when model output meets a trigger pattern, with a short timeout but no source-level sandbox or rollback; deployed host permissions are unknown. An optional provider code tool is attached in supported modes, but execution and isolation are external. The generic client separately exposes chat history and optional search, not configured as the benchmark's memory route ([RT-RTE-local-python](runtime.md), [RT-RTE-provider-code](runtime.md), [EPI-RTE-client-chat](epistemic.md), [EPI-RTE-client-search](epistemic.md)).
14:## Limitations
18:| No live operation, model outputs, or comparison establishing behavioral activation or benefit was supplied. | SRC-1; RT-RTE-cumulative-loop; RT-RTE-retrieval-synthesis; RT-RTE-cumulative-retrieval; RT-RTE-direct-retrieval; RT-RTE-full-history; EPI-CLM-performance-gains; EPI-CLM-zero-shot-learning | Registered repository at the frozen revision; prompts, implementation, tracked artifacts, with no provider execution or independent experiment | Whether supplied memory changes answers, improves future capacity, or causes reported performance gains | Inspectable runs and a controlled comparison that varies memory mechanisms while holding other relevant conditions fixed |
19:| Provider behavior and resolved model versions, including provider search and code execution, are outside the repository evidence. | RT-CMP-model; RT-RTE-provider-code; EPI-RTE-client-search | Provider request construction in SRC-1 only; no service traces or provider internals | Actual provider interpretation, search results, execution, isolation, persistence, and effects | Versioned provider traces and service contracts for the tested configuration |
20:| Retrieval vectors' provenance and the provenance/conditions of tracked datasets and result artifacts are not established. | MEM-OBJ-embedding-table; RT-OBJ-retrieval-context; EPI-CLM-performance-gains | Tracked CSV, data and result files and source references; no independently established artifact provenance | Retrieval relevance and independent reproduction or causal attribution of reported results | Provenance records, benchmark protocol, and reproducible artifact generation and evaluation |
21:| Local code execution uses the deployed Python process without a source-level sandbox or rollback; host permissions and any actual execution are unknown. | RT-RTE-local-python | Executor source only; no host configuration or execution trace | Scope of possible side effects and observed execution behavior | Deployed permission/isolation configuration and an inspectable execution trace |

item.text: The records support the main account of prompt delivery, post-curation scoring, memory routes, and unobserved effects. I found one wording issue: the synthesis describes extraction as requiring marked text and otherwise falling back, but the parser only requires the opening tag; if the closing tag is missing, it returns the remaining text. I’ll identify that as a blocker and check whether the limitations carry the unresolved conflicts.

### Synthesis verification

| public claim | qualifying or contrary record detail | judgment |
|---|---|---|
| Description: Dynamic Cheatsheet builds prompts from curated text or prior examples and carries returned text through caller or benchmark state; source wiring is visible, but use and benefit are unobserved. | "'`RT-OBJ-cheatsheet` and `RT-RTE-cumulative-loop` establish caller- or benchmark-carried text; `RT-RTE-retrieval-synthesis`, `RT-RTE-direct-retrieval`, and `RT-RTE-full-history` establish example context routes. Runtime evidence is implementation only; operation and behavioral effect are unobserved. | Supported and bounded. |
| Evidence is source inspection of the complete shipped repository; no live provider run or independent experiment was supplied. | `SRC-1` boundary covers the complete shipped repository and explicitly excludes live service behavior; `RT-RTE-cumulative-loop` records no live provider run. | Supported. |
| The system is an inference-time prompt and memory workflow; inspected code leaves model parameters untouched and passes natural-language text or prior input/output examples into later calls. | `RT-CMP-model` says parameters do not change in inspected inference code, while exact model version and provider resolution are not guaranteed; `MEM-OBJ-example-history` and `RT-OBJ-cheatsheet` identify text delivered to later calls. | Supported with the provider/version limit preserved by the source-level wording. |
| The model generates an answer and cumulative modes then ask it to propose replacement cheatsheet text; the prompt requests correctness assessment, but code does not check that assessment or gate the write on the benchmark target. | `RT-RTE-cumulative-loop` and `MEM-RTE-cumulative-write`: curator sees question, raw answer and prior text, not target/score; tagged output is accepted without content validation. | Supported. |
| The parser accepts text marked with `<cheatsheet>` and otherwise retains the old text. | `RT-RTE-cumulative-loop` and `MEM-RTE-cumulative-write` describe fallback when expected tags are absent. The epistemic source inspection of `dynamic_cheatsheet/utils/extractor.py` records that the parser checks for an opening marker; with no closing marker it returns all remaining text. | Blocker: wording implies both markers are required and fallback occurs otherwise. Correct the parser behavior description to match the opening-tag check and its missing-closing-tag behavior. IDs: `RT-RTE-cumulative-loop`, `MEM-RTE-cumulative-write`. |
| The benchmark carries returned text across questions and saves rows that can be loaded on continuation. | `RT-RTE-checkpoint-resume` and annotation on `RT-OBJ-run-checkpoint`: returned value is carried and latest row is restored; actual resume operation and file integrity are unobserved. | Supported as implementation behavior; no live recovery is claimed. |
| Its evaluator compares answers with task targets only after curation, updates counters, and does not admit, revise, or roll back text. | `EPI-RTE-benchmark-answer-check` says the evaluator runs after curation, affects counters only, and has no admission effect; `RT-RTE-cumulative-loop` agrees that score does not reach curator or rollback. | Supported. |
| Other modes rank prior pairs by cosine over fixed precomputed vectors, synthesize selected examples, append all prior examples, or use retrieved examples directly; linguistic history and numeric vectors are distinct parts. | `RT-RTE-retrieval-synthesis`, `RT-RTE-cumulative-retrieval`, `RT-RTE-direct-retrieval`, `RT-RTE-full-history`; reconciliation supersedes `EPI-OBJ-prior-pairs` with `MEM-OBJ-example-history` and `EPI-OBJ-retrieval-vectors` with `MEM-OBJ-embedding-table`. Vector provenance/relevance remain unknown. | Supported; canonical amended IDs are used. |
| These mechanisms establish delivery and retention paths, not reliance, correctness, or improved answers; README performance and learning claims remain unestablished, target scores do not feed curation, and learning/capacity/performance gains are undemonstrated. | `RT-RTE-cumulative-loop`, `MEM-RTE-cumulative-write`, `EPI-CLM-performance-gains`, `EPI-CLM-zero-shot-learning`: implementation shows delivery, but no run or causal comparison; scores do not gate writes. | Supported and carefully bounded. |
| Local Python execution can be triggered by model output, has a short timeout, and has no source-level sandbox or rollback; host permissions are unknown. | `RT-RTE-local-python` confirms trigger pattern, three-second timeout, no source sandbox/rollback, and unknown deployed permissions; no execution trace supplied. | Supported. |
| Optional provider code tooling is attached in supported modes, but execution and isolation are external. | `RT-RTE-provider-code`: source shows tool request construction; actual execution, sandbox and cleanup are outside the boundary. | Supported. |
| Generic client exposes separate chat history and optional search, not configured as the benchmark memory route. | `EPI-RTE-client-chat` and `EPI-RTE-client-search` establish separate generic-client routes; epistemic source boundary says wrapper does not configure Tavily search, with provider-native search-preview behavior possible but unobserved. | Supported; wording does not imply search is impossible through every model choice. |

### Blockers

- The parser description implies a closing `<cheatsheet>` marker is required and that any unmarked response falls back. `RT-RTE-cumulative-loop`; `MEM-RTE-cumulative-write`. Resolve by accurately describing the extractor'"'s opening-tag test, fallback when no opening tag exists, and behavior when the closing tag is absent.
EOF
"
